rest.description: Stateless request/response. Each request short-lived. Capacity is requests/sec.

ws.description: Long-lived bidirectional connections. Capacity is concurrent connections; throughput depends on msg/sec per connection.

msg_per_sec_per_conn.description: Average messages per second per connection (drives downstream load).

fanout_ratio.description: Fan-out factor: 1 message published → N delivered (pub/sub broadcast).

stream.description: Continuous data ingestion. Capacity is throughput; partitions/shards constrain parallelism.

avg_record_kb.description: Average record size in KB (drives partition count).

consumer_groups.description: Number of independent consumer groups (each reads full stream).

queueing_model.description: Latency penalty as utilization approaches capacity, using M/M/1 approximation.

rules.note: Mild queuing — p50 starts to climb.

p99_estimation.description: p99 estimation when only p50/p95 are known.

burst_modeling.description: Multiplier applied to load when simulating traffic spikes.

cold_start_models.description: Cold start latency added to p99 for serverless components when invocation rate is low.

load_unit_equivalence.description: QPS, RPS, and TPS are interchangeable units for the 'rest' workload. Use whichever the user said; treat them as the same number.
load_unit_equivalence.qps: Queries Per Second — DB / search context
load_unit_equivalence.rps: Requests Per Second — HTTP / API context
load_unit_equivalence.tps: Transactions Per Second — payments / OLTP context
load_unit_equivalence.rule: All map to the catalog's `capacity.rest` field.

sizing_heuristics.description: Back-of-envelope conversion rules from user-facing inputs (DAU, MAU, daily requests) to QPS/RPS/TPS. Source: standard capacity-planning practice (e.g., sujeet.pro/articles/capacity-planning-and-estimation).

dau_to_qps.shortcut: Daily requests / 10^5 (≈16% low, fine for BOTE)

peak_factor.description: Multiplier from average QPS to peak QPS. Always size against PEAK, not average.

read_write_split.description: Default read:write ratio for user-facing systems. Apply to compute and DB capacity separately.

cache_hit_defaults.description: 80/20 rule — 20% of data serves 80% of requests. Increasing 0→80% gives 5× DB headroom; 80→95% gives another 4×.

littles_law.use_for: Sizing connection pools, worker pool concurrency, file-descriptor budget.

tail_fanout.description: Fan-out amplifies tail latency. P(any of N exceeds p) = 1 - (1-p)^N.
tail_fanout.rule: If service fans out to N=100 backends and you want overall p99, each backend must hit p99.99.

provisioning_rule.explanation: Target 70% util at peak, then add N+2 for redundancy (planned drain + unplanned failure).
provisioning_rule.example: 100k peak QPS / 5k per server / 0.7 ≈ 29 servers, +2 = 31 servers

single_server_benchmarks.description: Order-of-magnitude per-server capacity. Use to sanity-check catalog values and to flag suspicious numbers.

availability_targets.description: Map availability % to downtime budget. Each extra '9' costs ~10× the engineering investment.

sharding_triggers.description: When to recommend sharding / partitioning in scenarios.
